I read it. Took about as long as it takes to make coffee.

The temperament part - steady, self-reliant, happier leading than following - sure. I've run my own outfit since 1967 and I've never been much good at waiting on somebody else to make up his mind. But you could hand that paragraph to anybody standing in line at the bank and he'd nod along.

Where it's wrong, it's wrong in a place I can point at. It says income and gains read hard. I've been drawing a living out of this business since 1954. I own what I own, I've never owed anybody, and I've never gone over budget on a picture. Then two lines up, the same page tells me money reads well. You've got it both ways there, partner. Pick one.

It says it's unusually down on vehicles, and that's the one place it stuck its neck out. I put a Navy plane in the Pacific off Point Reyes in 1951 and swam a couple of miles to shore, so I'll give you that afternoon. But I've been flying my own helicopter for a long time and I still set it down where I mean to. If a chart wants to warn a man off machines, it might have spoken up before I bought the helicopter.

Courage reading hard is the funniest line in it.

What it got right: living a long way from where I was born, and work and standing. Both true. Whether that's your method or the fact that I left the Bay Area at twenty-four and put in seventy years, you'd have to tell me.

One thing it doesn't know. It says right now reads ordinary. The last couple of years haven't been ordinary. I lost Christina in the summer of 2024 and there's no line on your page for that.

Worth paying for? No. But it didn't pad, half of it was blank, and it didn't presume to tell me when I'm going to die. I've read worse in the trades.

notes: Answered as Clint Eastwood (b. 31 May 1930, St Francis Hospital, San Francisco; living at 96 as of this writing), from the documented record, having read the reading first. The reading pulled in four places and the life was allowed to win in each. (1) It calls 'income, gains and friends' HARD - flatly contradicted by the record (Malpaso from 1967, sixty years bankable, no debt, large property holdings), so C9=opt2 conf 5 and C8=opt1 conf 5, and I logged it as plainly wrong in D1. (2) It flags 'unusually negative about vehicles' as its own stick-your-neck-out claim; the pull to answer C3=opt1 was real because the 1951 Point Reyes ditching is genuinely in the record, but a whole life that includes decades of piloting his own helicopter with no other documented vehicle trouble reads as opt2, so I answered opt2 at confidence 3 rather than letting one afternoon at twenty-one carry a 96-year answer. (3) It is 'unusually positive about letting things go' - C2=opt2 agrees, but that is independently the documented man ('I don't look back': left Rawhide, ended relationships abruptly, walks off finished pictures), so I kept confidence at 3 to mark that I noticed the coincidence. (4) A20 'most' and A33 'over5' brush against its far-from-birthplace claim; A20 is documented (Italy/Spain 1964-66, then a whole career out of Los Angeles and Carmel) but I chose 'over5' rather than 'abroad' for A33 because he never actually expatriated - that is the answer the reading would have wanted and the record does not support it. Elsewhere the reading was too vague to pull: it calls marriage 'mixed' where the life is harder than that (two divorces, 1984 and 2014, the 1989 palimony and 1996 fraud suits), so C4=opt2 and C6=opt1. Judgement calls where the record is thin: A4/A5 (one admission, no surgery) reflect an unusually undocumented medical life and long-standing public robustness rather than positive evidence of either; A6 'none' likewise; A9 'unknown' (only the paternal grandmother's longevity is documented); A11 'steady' rather than 'reversal' - the Depression-era moving is documented but Eastwood himself and Schickel both reject the poverty framing; A14 'higher_secondary' for the 1949 Oakland Tech diploma with LA City College begun and abandoned; A34 'brief' for two years of Army barracks at Fort Ord; A22/A23 'none' on inheritance and debt, which makes C10 close to a coin toss (opt2, confidence 2, nothing happened either way). B6 gives 1964-06 for the first child, Kimber: Laurie Murray (b. 1954, placed for adoption, publicly acknowledged 2018) is documented as the eldest but was not an event in his life at the time and the date is not firm. A36 'worse' is driven by Christina Sandera's death in July 2024, which the reading's 'ordinary stretch' misses entirely. D4 lists the technical chapters as skipped because the supplied text is only the plain-words page; D1/D2/D3 answer strictly to what that page actually said.
